history.p: In 1840 it was decided to raise a monument in memory of the newly deceased King Frederik VI at Skanderborg Slotsbanke (Skanderborg Castle Hill); however, the memorial with a bust made by Bertel Thorvaldsen was not finished until 1845. For the festivities on 31 July, B.S. Ingemann and Hans Christian Andersen were asked to write the texts, whereas Hartmann was requested to compose the music and was responsible for the practical matters. Unfortunately, the wind direction and a number of other circumstances made it almost impossible to hear the music, so that Hartmann had to write a rapport to the king who had attended the inauguration. Later the Festive March became extremely popular titled "Skanderborgmarsch" and was issued in a vast number of arrangements.

physDesc.physMedium: In library binding with the monogram of King Frederik IX. On the spine: "I.P.E. Hartmann / Skander-/ borg / Fest-/marsch / Part."; however, the volume contains the complete music for the unveiling of the monument in memory of Frederik VI at Skanderborg. Written in brown ink. Paper: 24 staves (pp. 1-14; and 18 staves pp. 46-49). The pagination in the upper l/r hand corners is sporadic, but later the pages have been numbered consecutively 1-49 apart from p. 46 which is doubled. On p. 16 at the end of the Marsh signed and end-dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann / 24. Julii 1845." On. p. 45 at the end of No. 3 signed and end-dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann / 18. Julii 1845." Pages 46 (bis)-49 contain sketches. On p. 48 Hartmann has written: "Partituret laant til Erslev d: 31. Decbr 1845." Horneman & Erslev published a version of the March for four-hand piano in April 1846. On the last pages with separate pagination Christian Barnekow's autograph score for the version with choir for Musikforeningens concert in honour of J.P.E. Hartmann on 7 May 1895.

Written in black ink. Paper: 10, 12 and 14 staves. The tenor parts are written on 2 pages, the bass parts on 4 pages. Some of the bass parts are signed by the singers: Keil, C.L. Bille 4/3 46, P.N Petersen, L. Jensen, Foersom 4/3 46.

annot.p: Version for mixed choir with new instrumentation: picc., 2 fl., 2 ob., 2 cl., 2 fg., 4 cor., 2 tr., 3 trb., tb., timp. gr.c & ptti., trgl.. vl.1, vl.2, vla., vcl., cb. This version was performed in Musikforeningen (The Music Society) in 1895 as a tribute to Hartmann on his 90th birthday. The added text is as follows: "Vær hilset i vor Tonehal, Nitiaarsmand! Guldalderskjald! / Hør din egen Harpes Toner fylde Festens Hus: / Klangen saa fuld! Strengen af Guld! evigt Sangbundens Brus. / Tungt er Tidens Fjed, / alt den mejer ned. / Dig har Vaaren stemt! / Dig har Høsten glemt! / Vær takket for Din Folkesang! for Vølvens Kvad og Hakons Lur, / for Psalmeklang bag Kirkens Mur; / for liden Kirstens Vise, / for Gurredrømmens Lyst, / for Havets Brise / i din Røst! / Dit Navn, dit Navn for os har Minder uden Tal. / Vær takket, du vor elskte gamle Skjald! / Takket vær, takket vær, tag vor Tak! / Lys og Sol i Alt, hvad du virked har Magt. / Din Kvæld nu smiler i Skjæret af Livsdagens Pragt. / Ej mørkne Skyers Mulm dens Fred, / til Solen træt gaar ned!"
